clue.text: Crew members pack sets of cards

parts.note: a pack of playing cards is a deck
the cards dealt to each player are hands

explanation.surface: Sailors pack away their card games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary seamen working on a ship's deck are members of its crew.

clue.text: Witty saying that's bowled Thomas over

indicators.note: bowled, read with the later word over, says knocked flat and turned the other way round
completes the phrase bowled over: the name is tipped end to end

parts.note: Tom is the short form of Thomas

explanation.surface: A clever quip has left Thomas astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled ... over' is split around Thomas and tells you to turn TOM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mot, as in bon mot, is a French-derived word for a clever remark.

clue.text: Very with it, former dictator offering health supplement?

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Something trendy that an old tyrant takes to stay healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins IT to V; 'with it' looks like a phrase meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill of essential nutrients is a typical example of something taken to supplement diet, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Present box, not opening

indicators.note: means the first letter of the box word is dropped

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox

explanation.surface: A gift box that has not been unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun meaning gift but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out or proffer it to someone.

clue.text: What may release smoke in YMCA's kitchen disastrously

indicators.note: something done disastrously goes badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fire in a hostel kitchen sends smoke billowing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall flue on a roof carries smoke up and away from the fire below.

clue.text: Ruin in a location for yachts

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or ruin it

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes at a sailing harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour with moorings for pleasure boats is where yachts are kept.

clue.text: Girl of a skeletal nature, really empty inside

indicators.note: puts the emptied word within the skeletal one

parts.note: bony means like bones or skeletal

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A painfully thin girl who is utterly hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'really empty' gives RY, the first and last letters of really.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing hedgerow plant name used as a female first name.

clue.text: No boy demands silly Victorian book

indicators.note: silly means foolish or nonsensical, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A daft request that a boy not be in a nineteenth-century novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens published this novel about a shipping firm in the 1840s, in Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Vehicle to travel, bringing load

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A vehicle setting off with a load on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by a ship or plane are its freight or load.

clue.text: Report offered by a cold nobleman

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A frosty aristocrat gives his version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A report and an account are both a description of what happened.

clue.text: Put down amateur

definitions.meaning: to place or set something down
non-professional, as in a non-clerical or non-expert person

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to set down; the other is the adjective for non-specialist, as in a layman.

clue.text: Terrible greed at an outdoor refreshment venue

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are badly scrambled

explanation.surface: Awful gluttony at an open-air cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air garden where tea and cakes are served is a place for refreshment outside.

clue.text: Daughter I have found in disreputable den

parts.note: contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A girl admits to being found in a seedy haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is only a link here, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a seedy bar or club.

clue.text: Animal about to land on the lady who grabs something moving?

parts.note: a cat is an animal
C stands for circa, Latin for about
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A cat is about to pounce on a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseball or cricket fielder who takes the ball in flight seizes a moving object.

clue.text: Meat for Noah's son

definitions.meaning: cured pork from a pig's leg
one of Noah's three sons in Genesis, alongside Shem and Japheth

explanation.definitionFit: Cured pig's thigh meat shares its name with the biblical son of Noah.

clue.text: Stake placed between two card players in French port

indicators.note: means the stake goes between the two players

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge
an ante is a stake put in before a poker hand

explanation.surface: Gamblers' money sits between two players in a French harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the Loire in western France, historically a major river port.

clue.text: Do press on somehow, given external funding

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep going however you can, now that someone else is paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Backed by a company or donor's money, as a charity walk might be.

clue.text: Mother entertains a female, one in criminal outfit

indicators.note: to entertain is to have guests inside, so the mother holds the rest

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother hosts a woman who belongs to a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian organised crime syndicate is the archetypal gangster organisation.

clue.text: Old gaoler imprisoning some number in country

indicators.note: means the country holds the number inside it, apt for a gaoler

parts.note: Turkey is a country
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A jailer of the past locking up a crowd somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey was the old term for a jailer, who turned the key in the cell lock.

clue.text: Fellow by exit finds vegetable

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a get-out is a way of escape or exit

explanation.surface: A man near the door comes across some greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat pea pod eaten whole is a kind of vegetable; the French name means eat-everything.

clue.text: Award when one gets a hundred in that examination

indicators.note: the word in here tells you to put the pair within the award

parts.note: a medal is an award
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A prize for whoever scores a hundred in the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' just joins I and C; 'in' places them inside MEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's check-up of one's health is a physical examination.

clue.text: Old, big-bellied and pompous

parts.note: rotund means round and plump

explanation.surface: A description of an ageing, paunchy, self-important man.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes a bombastic, high-flown speaking style.

clue.text: After revolution a map includes a new country

indicators.note: means the turned-round words take the rest inside them
after a revolution the words are turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: After an uprising, a redrawn map shows a new nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A MAP turned round gives PAMA; AN goes inside it after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic famous for its canal.

clue.text: Month in which to see king and queen combine harmoniously

indicators.note: says the royal pair are seen inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
R is for rex, Latin for king
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A spring wedding month where king and queen unite.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry flavours or colours is to blend them well together.

clue.text: Shock when gimmicky performance falls short

indicators.note: means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a stunt is an attention-grabbing feat

explanation.surface: Dismay when a showy act fails to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or shock them.

clue.text: Lunch always includes this drink

indicators.note: the two words hold the drink within them

explanation.surface: A midday meal always comes with a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is slang for tea, from the Chinese word.
